---
title: "Validation"
---

`stokesjx` is compared with three independent references: the Fortran code CODE-A, a
second solver in high-precision arithmetic, and analytical solutions. The derivatives are
checked by Taylor tests and dot products. For each reference, the bound of the test
comes first and the measured agreement second.

## The error metric

The values are compared with the metric `e_l`: per degree, the largest difference over
the source nodes divided by the largest reference value.

## Fortran CODE-A

The golden output of CODE-A comes from runs under CODE-A's own switches. These switches
are a uniform gravity of 10 m/s², the material of an interval at its upper node, and
equal weights of the radial integral. `stokesjx` reproduces these switches in a test-only mode of its low
layer. The golden data is a reduced, checksummed set in `tests/golden/`. The Fortran
itself is not distributed.

| Case | Bound | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| isoviscous, all 50 degrees | `1e-12` | 2.6e-14 |
| hager4 viscosity | `1e-12` | 2.7e-14 |
| smooth viscosity | `1e-12` | 1.8e-13 |
| TALA and no slip | `1e-12` | at most 3.0e-13 |

## The mpmath reference

A second solver computes the kernels at 50 to 250 digits with mpmath
(`tests/reference_mpmath.py`). It uses the single product of the propagators, the
algorithm that needs high precision, and not the sweeps of the package. The agentic coding
tools wrote it from the same equations as the package. It is independent in its algorithm
and its arithmetic, not in its authorship. The references that no tool wrote are the
CODE-A output and the analytical solutions of Kramer, Davies and Wilson (2021).

| Case | Bound | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| moderate cases, degrees 1 to 200 | `1e-12` | at most 8.5e-14 |
| raw frame at `l = 1` (split core) | `1e-12` | 3.1e-13 |
| stiff lid and ten decades of viscosity | `1e-11` | 1.2e-12 (stiff lid, at `l = 1`), 3.6e-13 (ten decades) |
| 32 flag combinations | `1e-12` | at most 4.6e-13 |
| the viscosity cut | `1e-12` | at most 1e-13 (2e-14 typical) |

## Analytical solutions

The reference is the analytical solutions of Kramer, Davies and Wilson (2021) through the
package `assess`. They cover an isoviscous shell, delta and smooth forcing, free slip and
no slip, with a uniform gravity and no self-gravitation. Bound `1e-12`, measured 1.2e-14.

## Derivatives

Every Taylor case passes the policy of [the derivatives page](gradients.qmd#taylor-tests),
with both signs and both modes, and every negative control fails. The two Taylor cases of
the integration tests have the corrected rates 1.997 and 2.000. The jvp/vjp dot products
agree to `1e-12` (1e-14 typical).

## Errors of CODE-A that stokesjx fixes

| CODE-A | stokesjx |
|---|---|
| `grav()` returns 10 m/s² everywhere. | The gravity is integrated from `rho0` and the core mass. A uniform `g` is a flag. |
| The free-air kernel uses `G M / R^2`, everything else 10 m/s². | The gravity anomaly comes from the geoid and the surface `g` of the profile. |
| The viscosity and the density of a layer are those of its upper node. | The material of an interval is the mean of its two nodes. A jump is a node pair. |
| The radial integral gives every node the same weight. | The trapezoid weights of the node table. |
| The degree-1 geoid kernel is set to zero; the other degree-1 kernels are not. | Degree 1 is in the centre-of-mass frame for all outputs. |
| The Sylvester formula removes close eigenvalues; 128-bit reals for one product of propagators. | Exact interval exponentials and two orthonormalised sweeps per degree, stable in float64 at every degree. |
| The admittance kernel is a ratio of two kernels. | The admittance comes from the field coefficients. |
| The `SPHCO` header says "Cnm, Snm(m<0)", but each line holds C and then S. | The readers parse the data order. |
| The compressible term is a one-sided difference of `rho0`. | The TALA term comes from the same interval data as the rest. |

## Where the tests run

One test run checks every reference: `python -m pytest -n 8` runs every test. On the
author's machine every test runs: 1102 tests pass in 327 s.

The CI job on the self-hosted runners of the repository runs every test that needs
neither `legacy/` nor lovejx. It skips 25 tests:

- 12 tests that need the Fortran reference (`legacy/`, not distributed);
- the 13 tests that compare with lovejx: 10 tests of `stokesjx.sh` against
  `lovejx.sealevel.sht` and 3 tests of the background gravity against lovejx. CI does
  not install lovejx, because lovejx is not on PyPI and its repository is not public
  yet.

The other tests of `stokesjx.sh` run in CI. They check the conventions against scipy and
against the formula of CODE-A, the Gauss-Legendre round trip, the conversions and the
degree power.

## What the comparison does not establish

The comparison with CODE-A uses CODE-A's own discrete model. It checks the solver, not
the choice of the model. The comparisons against published values are not done yet
([open points](open-points.qmd)).
